ROLE: Allocate an empty broker registry, its initial session slot array and its reusable encode scratch buffer, reporting success only when every owned allocation exists.

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: registry object being created: sessions array, count, capacity and scratch buffer

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: scratch buffer initialised empty so route_publish can reuse it

FUNC.NAME: free
FUNC.ROLE: release partial allocations on the failure paths

FUNC.NAME: buffer_init
FUNC.ROLE: initialise the scratch buffer to empty with no storage

VAR.NAME: BROKER_INITIAL_SESSION_CAP
VAR.ROLE: number of session slots allocated up front

VAR.NAME: struct broker
VAR.ROLE: out_broker receives the only owning pointer to the new registry

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_init
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; data becomes NULL, len 0 and cap 0, so nothing is stored yet
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the buffer owns no storage until buffer_reserve succeeds; the broker owns the buffer struct itself

LOGIC.INPUT: out_broker: caller-provided output slot for the single owning registry pointer.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If out_broker is NULL return -1. 2. *out_broker = NULL so a caller ignoring the result cannot use an indeterminate pointer. 3. b = calloc(1, sizeof *b); if b is NULL return -1. 4. b->sessions = malloc(BROKER_INITIAL_SESSION_CAP * sizeof *b->sessions); if it is NULL, free(b) and return -1 (no partial object escapes). 5. b->count = 0; b->cap = BROKER_INITIAL_SESSION_CAP. 6. buffer_init(&b->scratch) so the scratch buffer starts empty and its storage is allocated lazily by the first route_publish. 7. *out_broker = b; return 0.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 0 with *out_broker pointing to an empty registry (count 0, capacity BROKER_INITIAL_SESSION_CAP, empty scratch, no I/O descriptors). -1 with *out_broker == NULL when out_broker is NULL or an allocation failed; all memory allocated by the failing attempt has been freed, so the caller has nothing to clean up.
INVARIANTS_USED: the registry starts with no sessions and no descriptors of its own; the execution layer supplies the listener
every allocation made here is reachable through out_broker on success and freed on failure
the scratch buffer is broker-owned and reusable, so fan-out does not allocate a buffer per publish
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: out_broker points to writable storage of type struct broker *.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: either the caller owns a fully initialised empty registry, or no registry exists and no allocation was leaked.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Called once before the reactor starts; no concurrent access.

INPUT.injected_failure: malloc of the session slot array fails
